label: ExtremeSwitching X465-24MU-24W
description: ExtremeSwitching X465-24MU-24W - 24x 100M/1G/2.5G/5G BASE-T RJ-45 with 802.3bt Type 3 60 W PoE+ (ports 1:1-1:24) plus 24x 10/100/1000BASE-T RJ-45 with 802.3bt Type 4 90 W PoE+ (ports 1:25-1:48), one empty VIM5 uplink slot, two 40G dedicated stacking ports (unpopulated), rear RJ-45 console and a 1G out-of-band management port; 696 Gbps aggregated switch bandwidth, 517.9 Mpps.

fabric.note: Extreme states 696 aggregated switch bandwidth and 517.9 frame forwarding rate for the X465-24MU-24W (datasheet Performance and Scale table, https://extr-p-001.sitecorecontenthub.cloud/api/public/content/df5d3e48f1834936bc0d1caeae677c02?v=f38c16b6). The vendor figure counts the VIM5 uplink capacity and the two 40G stacking ports as well as the front panel, so it is larger than the aggregate of the Ethernet ports modelled here; nothing on the modelled ports is capped by it.

notes: Port census from the datasheet and the installation guide, which is explicit that ports 1-24 offer multi-rate with 60 W PoE support and ports 25-48 support 90 W but do not offer multi-rate: 24 x 100M/1/2.5/5G Type 3 60 W plus 24 x 10/100/1000BASE-T Type 4 90 W, all MACsec-capable on the 1G half. Modelled as one template for 1:1-1:24 and 24 explicit ports 1:25-1:48 so each half carries its own PoE class. VIM5 slot empty: VIM5-4X (4x 1/10G SFP+), VIM5-4XE (4x 1/10G SFP+, LRM/MACsec), VIM5-4Y / VIM5-4YE (4x 10/25G SFP28), VIM5-2Y (2x 25G SFP28), VIM5-2Q (2x 40G QSFP+). The module is not hot-swappable and its ports are not modelled here, so the box is the bare chassis. S1 and S2 are 2x 40G QSFP+ stacking ports on the front panel, 42 Gbps per link under SummitStack-V160; the stacking-support option is always enabled on the X465 and these are native stacking-only ports, so they are not modelled as Ethernet data ports. Console is the rear-panel RJ-45 serial port (plus a USB micro-B console that takes priority when connected), and the rear also carries a 10/100/1000BASE-T out-of-band management port, modelled as mgmt. Quad-core 2.1 GHz x86, 8 GB DDR4, 8 GB eMMC, 3 fan modules, system power 332 W. Idle 96 W, maximum 3941 W with both halves fully loaded. Sources: https://extr-p-001.sitecorecontenthub.cloud/api/public/content/df5d3e48f1834936bc0d1caeae677c02?v=f38c16b6, https://cdn.blueally.com/netsolutionstore/datasheets/switches/x465-series-data-sheet.pdf, https://documentation.extremenetworks.com/ExtremeSwitching%20Installation%20Guide%20for%20Switches%20Using%20ExtremeXOS%20Version%2030/Wired_Hardware/ExtremeSwitching_Installation_Guide_for_Switches_Using_ExtremeXOS_Version_30/topics/extremeswitching_x465_series_switches_technical_specifications.shtml, https://documentation.extremenetworks.com/ExtremeSwitching%20Installation%20Guide%20for%20Switches%20Using%20ExtremeXOS%20Version%2030/Wired_Hardware/ExtremeSwitching_Installation_Guide_for_Switches_Using_ExtremeXOS_Version_30/topics/extremeswitching_x465_series_switches.shtml, https://documentation.extremenetworks.com/ExtremeSwitching%20Installation%20Guide%20for%20Switches%20Using%20ExtremeXOS%20Version%2030/Universal_Hardware/Universal_Hardware_Common/topics/build_stacks/extremeswitching_x465_stacking.shtml.

poe.note: 3468 W with two 2000 W PSUs on 200-240 V, the installation guide figure, which applies an 8 W derating for the 2000 W supply where the datasheet still prints 3476 W. The two halves do not share one standard: ports 1-24 are Type 3 at 60 W, ports 25-48 Type 4 at 90 W, so 24 x 60 W + 24 x 90 W = 3600 W is more than the largest stated budget - the box cannot run every port at its maximum class at once. With a 1100 W PSU the budget is 768 W, with 715 W it is 383 W (https://documentation.extremenetworks.com/ExtremeSwitching%20Installation%20Guide%20for%20Switches%20Using%20ExtremeXOS%20Version%2030/Wired_Hardware/ExtremeSwitching_Installation_Guide_for_Switches_Using_ExtremeXOS_Version_30/topics/extremeswitching_x465_series_switches_technical_specifications.shtml).
